note_tweet.text:
There's a way to find 100x Meme coins that insiders call a shortcut.  
This method is rock-solid—once you've got it down pat, you can pretty much skip the other strategies.

1 → Pick a coin that blew up in the last market cycle  
Doesn't matter if it surged 4,500x or 750x before.  
Even if it's worthless now, that's fine—even better, actually.

2 → Find the top 20 wallets that bought in earliest  
Open up the GMGN page for that coin and list out the first buyers.  
If it's not on Solana, head to Etherscan and check the contract's early transactions.

GMGN: https://t.co/jEbUTw6ZYa

3 → Pick the wallets that are still trading now  
Out of those 20, most stopped trading ages ago.  
Check which ones have been buying or selling in the last 30 days—usually just three to five left.

4 → Filter out the bot wallets  
If the trades are spaced just seconds apart, that's a bot.  
Tracking bots is pointless—we can't outrun them anyway.

5 → See what the remaining wallets have been up to lately  
Check what coins they've bought in the last 30 days, how much they grabbed, and if they're still holding.  
This page is the real heart of the method.

6 → Watch for projects that multiple wallets are buying at once  
One wallet jumping on a coin solo? Could just be luck.  
But three different wallets piling into the same one? That's your signal.

7 → Evaluate the coin using your own scoring system  
Score the tokens that made the cut.  
Even if a wallet made bank on it, if it doesn't hit at least 9 out of 10, steer clear.

That's the seven steps.

Now, why this method works so well.  
Folks who nail 100x gains fall into two camps:  
Either they got lucky, or they've got a battle-tested playbook.  
Luck-based wins? Tough to repeat.  
But the method-savvy crowd? They run the same playbook every cycle.

Your job is to track down those who've cashed in big before and see what they're buying now.

Too many people wait for someone else to shill a coin—only jumping in when the crowd says so.  
With this approach, you don't wait for tips from anyone.  
Those sharp players who position early? Their wallets are already on your radar.

One thing to watch out for.  
Buying the same coin as a wallet doesn't guarantee the same profits.  
They might throw in $100K while you've only got $1K—totally different risk levels.

And don't forget:  
Anyone can see when a wallet buys in. But when they sell? That's the real secret sauce.  
Buys are public; sells often stay hidden.

Give it a shot today.  
Grab an old coin, unearth 20 early wallets, pick three to keep tabs on.  
Drop in the comments what you dig up.

I'm building my own watchlist too.  
Get hands-on and try it out.
